ai_technology: VirTues-M2; multimodal vision transformer and learned cell-signature transfer

evidence.ai_role: A marker-aware multimodal transformer learned joint H&E and spatial-proteomics representations. Clustering enabled annotation-free cell-state discovery; Cox screening selected survival-linked populations and random-forest classifiers transferred their membership to another cohort.
evidence.tested: Signature selection used 737 discovery patients and evaluation used 316 held-out patients. Combined signatures reached C-index 0.646 and hazard ratio 3.09 in the test set. Unchanged signature classifiers transferred to 39 external patients; combined signatures had C-index 0.636 and hazard ratio 2.87 (p=0.039).
evidence.unknown: Retrospective survival associations do not establish causation or treatment-response prediction. External validation is small; the H&E-only external signature was not significant at p<0.05. Test patients used pre-specified tertiles, whereas external patients used a median split. Prospective clinical utility and robustness require further evaluation.

organization: EPFL; University Hospital Zurich; University of Zurich; University of Bern

source_review.scope: Primary arXiv HTML relevant model description, spatial biomarker discovery Methods, Figure 6 Results and clinical limitations; primary submission history. Supplements and other benchmark tasks not audited.

summary: A November 23, 2026 preprint reports that VirTues-M2 learned joint tissue morphology and spatial-protein representations to discover survival-associated cellular signatures in lung cancer. Signatures selected on 737 patients stratified survival in 316 held-out patients and transferred without retraining to a separate 39-patient cohort. Low-risk signatures marked organized immune-rich neighborhoods; high-risk signatures marked more disorganized tumor-rich tissue. These are retrospective prognostic associations with small external validation and no demonstrated treatment benefit.
title: Multimodal AI finds lung-cancer tissue signatures associated with survival
